name: Fenvik Soursop-Ginger Root
description: An unlicensed street brand produced in Tier 1's industrial district using synth-soursop and real ginger root sourced from urban grow-ops. Sold in unmarked amber bottles with hand-applied labels.
flavor_profile: Creamy, tropical soursop sweetness followed by a real ginger heat that builds slowly. No artificial aftertaste. Heavy carbonation. Warm and complex for a Shelf product.
cultural_context: Fenvik is one of Meridian 88's most respected street brands precisely because it has refused to license or scale. The bottles are refillable — buyers bring back empties for a Φ0.10 credit — and the operation employs entirely Shelf-resident workers. Fenvik has become a minor symbol of Tier 1 economic self-determination.
story_hooks: A corponation has sent a legal team to shut down Fenvik's unlicensed production — but the operation is protected by the surrounding community, and the legal team is finding that enforcement in Tier 1 is more complicated than expected.
Fenvik's ginger supply comes from a rooftop grow-op that is also producing something else — the soda operation is an unwitting cover, and the people running the grow-op need it to stay that way.
A Tier 4 food publication wants to run a feature on Fenvik as 'authentic Shelf culture' — and the Fenvik operators must decide if the exposure will help or destroy what they've built.
